claim_boundary: Close Cardueae structural analog; involucral spines are not identical to Cirsium phyllary posture.
Legitimate pollinators were not more likely to visit spineless heads; does not exclude effects on handling duration or pollen transfer.
Bees and flies spent about 20% more time per visit on spineless heads; duration is not equivalent to visit frequency or plant fitness.
Spine removal reduced percentage of filled seeds by 22%; direct Cardueae manipulation but not a Cirsium phyllary-posture effect.
Direct Asteraceae orientation manipulation; effect size must not be transported to Cirsium.
No pollinator preference was observed between manipulated erect and natural nodding capitula.
Water and UV-B seriously reduced pollen viability; elongated involucral bracts also sheltered pollen from UV-B. Mechanism analog, not a Cirsium effect.
Nodding orientation did not modify internal thermal conditions in this system; does not rule out thermal timing in other taxa.
